persons.name: Leslie
persons.harm: Her boyfriend controlled, isolated and deceived her, exploited her financially, and killed her adopted son. She describes enduring grief, guilt and harassment by his family.

quotes.quote: I never thought he would hurt me or Jace, but I was afraid he would threaten to kill himself and he would never leave me alone.
As it was right now, I could not afford to make it in this house without him. I couldn't afford the mortgage on my own.
I hate, hate, hate confrontation and awkward conversations. I will do anything to appease anyone in order to avoid them, but I couldn't hold this in.

contacts.what_happened_next: She went before a judge two days later.
contacts.notes: Investigative safeguard also separated her from her dying child; no punitive motive inferred.

contacts.what_institution_did: Allowed her back at hospital.
contacts.quote: She had to go before a judge two days later and the judge then allowed her to be at the hospital.

contacts.quote: same thing. So I think that helped me to be able to say, okay, this is because of him, not because of her.

contacts.quote: They were a big support and it felt like they really wanted to honor Jace and wanted justice for him.

contacts.what_institution_did: Advised liability was unlikely.
contacts.quote: I did ask the DA if they thought I should pursue legal action against him. And she said that because I had taken Jace to the doctor so much and no one suspected or reported anything that she didn't think they would find him liable.
contacts.notes: Advice, not adjudicated medical liability.

contacts.what_institution_did: Returned guilty verdict for child abuse murder.
contacts.quote: The defendant is guilty and fixed punishment at life and a fine of $10,000.

persons.outcome_quote: You have been found guilty and will spend the rest of your life in prison.

No report to a platform about online harassment is described. Medical contacts about the child are in P02. Outcome correction: later incarceration supplied accountability, but no institutional action is shown ending this person's narrated coercion, threats or bereavement. coder_notes: All four season chunks read consecutively in full, including trailer, ads and season-assigned Data Points: Child Abuse. That educational episode contains no individual cases. INDEX was read in full. Two potentially relevant unassigned specialist episodes read in full supplied no additional season-17 stories. Other index entries did not identify a continuation of these people. Every death-related outcome distinguishes justice from protection of the deceased. The surviving bereaved relatives are included because their own harm and aftermath are narrated; incarceration is accountability but does not demonstrate protection from the narrated bereavement. Medical treatment for a specific illness alone does not establish a report of abuse: parental-neglect and bereavement disclosure uncertainties are marked. No conclusion about actual reporting is drawn from hypothetical reporting conversations in closing arguments. Repeated accounts of the same contact are deduplicated; undated groups of visits/appellate decisions are explicitly grouped. Quotes preserve transcription except perpetrator names replaced with [perpetrator]. not_stated quotations establish the narrated harm, not an inferred reason for silence. Source timestamp identifies start of the quoted minute. No other coder work, branches, issues or PRs were opened during coding.
